# Hierarchical, Graph-Based, and Adaptive Structures

Also called: Adaptive Gaussian Partitioning, Test-Time Gaussian Deformation

## Overview
This family addresses the limitations of standard 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) regarding scalability, hardware constraints, and aliasing artifacts. It introduces methods to partition scenes into manageable regions, adaptively select Gaussian subsets for inference, and deform primitives to match specific sampling rates. Unlike standard 3DGS, which uses a fixed set of Gaussians, these methods employ dynamic structures (graphs, selectors, or deformable fields) to optimize memory, quality, or rendering fidelity at varying scales.

## Shared principles
All methods in this family operate on the standard 3D Gaussian representation defined by mean position $\mathbf{X}$, covariance matrix $\Sigma$ (parameterized by rotation $\mathbf{R}$ and scaling $\mathbf{S}$), opacity $\alpha$, and spherical harmonics coefficients $\mathbf{SH}$ . The rendering process follows the standard differentiable splatting pipeline, where pixel color $C$ is computed by blending ordered Gaussians overlapping the pixel:
$$ C = \sum_{i \in N} c_i \alpha_i \prod_{j=1}^{i-1} (1 - \alpha_j) $$


The core distinction lies in the modification of the Gaussian set $\{G_k\}$ or the rendering context:
1.  **Partitioning:** The scene is divided into disjoint subsets (regions) with independent Gaussian sets, connected via a graph structure .
2.  **Selection:** A subset of Gaussians is chosen based on a target ratio or importance, often using learnable selectors .
3.  **Deformation:** Gaussian parameters (position, scale, color) are optimized at test time to adapt to specific zoom factors or resolutions .

## Subtopics

### [TraGraph-GS](14454-tragraph-gs.md)
TraGraph-GS handles large-scale scenes by decoupling the scene into local regions and a global representation using a camera connectivity graph [14454-tragraph-gs.md]. It constructs a graph $G=(V, E, w)$ where vertices are images and edge weights are feature match counts [14454-tragraph-gs.md]. The graph is segmented into $k$ balanced, connected regions using BFS [14454-tragraph-gs.md]. Local Gaussians are trained with a multi-view constraint ($L_{mv}$) using patch matching to improve geometry in textureless regions [14454-tragraph-gs.md]. A multi-scale constraint $\gamma(\mu)$ adjusts Gaussian scales based on distance from the camera center [14454-tragraph-gs.md]. For novel views, it uses progressive rendering with matching scores to blend local and global Gaussians, eliminating boundary artifacts [14454-tragraph-gs.md].

### FlexGS
FlexGS enables a single trained model to adapt to varying computational constraints at inference time [16110-flexgs.md]. It uses a learnable Gaussian selector to choose a subset of Gaussians based on a target ratio $e$, and a ratio-dependent transformation field to displace selected Gaussians to compensate for missing details [16110-flexgs.md]. The selection uses a Gumbel-Softmax approximation during training to allow gradient-based optimization of discrete selection variables [16110-flexgs.md]. This avoids the need for separate model generations or costly retraining for different hardware constraints [16110-flexgs.md].

### [Mipmap-GS](16893-mipmap-gs.md)
Mipmap-GS eliminates aliasing artifacts (zoom-in spikes and zoom-out thickness) by deforming pre-trained Gaussians at test time [16893-mipmap-gs.md]. It generates scale-specific pseudo ground-truth images by applying mipmap-like resizing (super-resolution for zoom-in, bilinear interpolation for zoom-out) to base renderings [16893-mipmap-gs.md]. The Gaussians are optimized via gradient descent to minimize the L2 loss between the rendered image and the pseudo ground-truth [16893-mipmap-gs.md]. Active pruning is performed every 100 iterations to maintain compactness [16893-mipmap-gs.md].

## Background
Standard 3D Gaussian Splatting [9128-3d-gaussian-splatting-implementation-details.md] struggles with large-scale scenes due to memory constraints, fixed hardware requirements, and aliasing artifacts at varying zoom levels. TraGraph-GS [14454-tragraph-gs.md] addresses large-scale scalability through graph-based partitioning. FlexGS [16110-flexgs.md] addresses hardware adaptability through learnable selection. Mipmap-GS [16893-mipmap-gs.md] addresses aliasing through test-time deformation. These methods extend the base 3DGS implementation [9128-3d-gaussian-splatting-implementation-details.md] to handle specific deployment and quality challenges.
